newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian newspapers praise Deng's legacy.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian newspapers praise Deng's legacy.

text.p: Indonesian newspapers on Friday praised late Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiaoping for instituting reforms which set his country on the road to stability and economic growth.
"The benefits of Deng's reforms went far beyond China's borders," the English-language Jakarta Post said in an editorial.

"The prosperity that the Asia-Pacific region -- including Indonesia -- has enjoyed these last 20 years could be attributed indirectly, but not insignificantly, to China's political stability and a rapidly growing economy under Deng," it said.
Deng died late on Wednesday from respiratory failure at the age of 92.
The influential Indonesian-language Kompas newspaper said: "Unlike Mao (Zedong) who tended to be idealistic, Deng was very pragmatic in economic development.
"His pragmatic approach was obvious in July 1962 when he said: 'It does not matter if a cat is black or white, as long as it catches mice'."
Bisnis Indonesia, the country's largest business newspaper, predicted Deng's death would not create a power struggle in China as happened after the death of Mao Zedong.

"The greatest threat for (Deng's chosen successor) Jiang Zemin in fact comes from the economic reformation itself, with the danger that it could boomerang and be used by his opponents as a pretext to damage the reforms," it said.
President Suharto on Thursday conveyed Indonesia's condolences to China on Deng's death and said his reforms had brought prosperity to China's 1.2 billion people.
Indonesia resumed diplomatic ties with China in 1990 after severing them following a 1965 coup attempt blamed on the Indonesian Communist Party (PKI), which is still officially banned.
